segments.content:
Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 144: Your Water, My Water

"When the dark night passes, on the horizon"

"I am that ray of light"

"Warming myself and giving strength to others"

At the entrance of the gymnasium, Li Luo listened to Yan Zhusheng sing this song, feeling a little dazed for a moment.

Just yesterday, he had stood in the very spot where Yan Zhusheng was standing now, singing the same song to Ying Chanxi.

At that time, he was extremely confident and bold. After the tempering of the parent-teacher conference and the sports meet opening ceremony, he was already adept at this kind of all-venue performance.

But now, standing where Ying Chanxi had stood yesterday, listening to another person sing the same song to him, was a completely different feeling.

A very special feeling.

Especially after Yan Zhusheng finished the song and simply left a "Good luck" into the microphone, it made everyone find it even more intriguing.

Only Li Luo knew immediately that she was saying it to him.

Although this thought might seem a bit narcissistic, a bit arrogant to outsiders, it was the truth.

Of course, besides him, Xu Yinghuan, who was sitting in the stands, also guessed it instantly. The corners of her mouth lifted like crazy, feeling like she had just witnessed another sweet moment.

And among the students of Class Eight, some things had long been circulating in private. Yan Zhusheng's action at this moment only served to confirm that fact once again.

As for the students from other classes and grades, it was a different matter entirely.

They had no idea about the relationship between Yan Zhusheng and Li Luo; they only felt that this girl was so confident she seemed to shine.

In an instant, she was etched into the hearts of countless people, becoming a ray of light that would be hard to erase from their youth.

Perhaps when they reached middle age, occasionally drinking and reminiscing about the past, looking back on their high school years, they would have long forgotten the problems they did and the exams they took.

But they would remember that there was such a girl who had once left an imprint in their hearts with a single song.

Even if the two of them never had any interaction during their high school years.

In his past life, even if Li Luo could have really gotten into Fuyi High, he would probably have been just like these people. But in this life, things were a bit different.

Li Luo chuckled softly, an inexplicable emotion flowing through his heart. After the song ended, its melody lingering in the air, he finally turned and went back into the gymnasium, lined up to register for the 3000-meter race, and followed Xu Youyu, who was leading the team, towards the starting line.

Because this was already the final event among all the student competitions, the school specially lifted the restrictions on the stands, allowing students to enter and exit freely to watch from the grass field and beside the track.

Thus, as the first-year 3000-meter race was about to begin, many people from each class came down, crowding thickly around the starting and finish lines.

Led by Yan Zhusheng, quite a few students from Class Eight had gathered over.

"Go, Class President!"

"Go, Wei Chun, too!"

Zhu Yufei and Zhang Guohuang shouted from the side.

Li Luo looked over in that direction, and his gaze quickly met Yan Zhusheng's.

Yan Zhusheng didn't shout "good luck," because she had already said it. So at this moment, she simply waved at him and then silently gave him a thumbs-up.

Li Luo couldn't help but laugh. Then, under the teacher's arrangement, he stepped onto the starting line, stood in a row with the others, and waited for the start signal.

In the stands, Ying Chanxi, whose movement was restricted due to her injured knee, looked eagerly at the crowded scene below, pouting a little with unhappiness.

Qiao Xinyan, beside her, saw this and could only comfort her, "It's quite good in the stands too. You can get a view of the whole situation, isn't that clearer?"

Ying Chanxi pouted, thinking that this was only a small part of the reason for her bad mood.

But she was too embarrassed to say more to Qiao Xinyan, so she could only nod and silently wait for the race to begin.

Meanwhile, Li Luo, standing at the starting line, saw that the teacher wasn't ready to start yet, so he glanced left and right but didn't spot any guys who looked like sports students.

However, Lu Wei from the class next door grinned and squeezed into the spot beside Li Luo, looking like he was determined to compete with him.

As for Liu Shaowen on the other side, he didn't take the 3000-meter race to heart at all. His goal was just to finish the whole course, so he was quite relaxed at the moment, chatting with Li Luo.

"Don't worry, Li Luo. Ying Chanxi is in our class. It's fine even if her leg is injured. Our classmates will take good care of her."

"I'm not worried about that," Li Luo replied casually, feeling a bit unable to comprehend Liu Shaowen's line of thinking. Why had this kid been so enthusiastic towards him recently?

Finally, the teacher was about ready. He raised a small flag toward the finish line to signal, then had the runners on this side get ready.

"On your marks."

"Set—"

"Go!"

With a simple command, Li Luo shot out from the starting line.

It was probably thanks to his daily morning and night runs recently, plus the school's long morning break exercise routine, that Li Luo's physical fitness was excellent.

If it were his thirty-five-year-old body from his past life, Li Luo found it hard to imagine he could sprint out at this speed and still not feel much weight or fatigue, but rather a sense of lightness.

With a push of his feet, he felt as if he were flying forward, his entire body filled with a power called youth.

Immediately, Li Luo stayed in the leading pack.

For this 3000-meter race, each class theoretically had two registration slots, but in reality, it wasn't full.

Some classes really had no one willing to participate, so maybe only one person signed up.

So in the end, there were only about twenty-five or twenty-six people on the field.

In the first half of the lap right after the race started, these twenty-some people immediately stratified.

The ones furthest behind were clearly those who were just there to make up the numbers, many of whom were even a bit chubby, completely unsuited for long-distance running.

It was simply because no one else in their class would do it that they were forced into this event, brought out as complete cannon fodder.

This was the third-tier group, numbering about seven or eight people.

Ahead of them was the large second-tier pack, where Wei Chun was.

There were a good twelve or thirteen people in this group, starting from an initial crowd, and later forming a long line, following each other closely.

As for the first tier, it consisted of four or five people including Li Luo, who clearly had pretty good endurance and had been at the front from the very beginning.

When they reached the second lap, Li Luo was originally following a student in front of him, but then Lu Wei came out of nowhere, insisting on squeezing into second place.

Li Luo didn't fight him for it, happy to have someone block the wind for him, so he simply ran silently behind Lu Wei.

But in reality, Lu Wei had purely burned a lot of stamina to charge up from the second-tier pack.

It was all to catch up to Li Luo's pace.

He hadn't expected Li Luo to have some skill, to be so far ahead right at the start of a 3000-meter race. How could he stand for that? He immediately sprinted up.

He even specifically chose a spot where Gao Yuqin was watching on the grass field.

When he passed Li Luo's position right in front of Gao Yuqin, a surge of pride welled up deep inside him, and his running gained much more vigor.

Li Luo didn't really care and just followed behind Lu Wei.

But Ying Chanxi in the stands clenched her fists and muttered under her breath, "What are you doing? Someone passed you and you're not passing them back? I'm so anxious."

A 3000-meter long-distance race, on a 400-meter track, was a full seven and a half laps long.

Li Luo was in no hurry. He consistently adjusted his rhythm, maintaining a pace slightly faster than his usual morning runs, and evenly kept his breathing and stride.

In contrast, Lu Wei, running ahead, would occasionally slow down on the straightaways because he was running out of steam, only to be caught up by Li Luo, and then he would have to grit his teeth and accelerate again.

After this repeated three or four times, by the time they reached the fourth lap, Lu Wei was already panting heavily, drenched in sweat, his entire rhythm in disarray.

By the fifth lap, his feet felt as if they were filled with lead, and Li Luo easily overtook him.

And when he wanted to speed up again to pass back, he found that his feet wouldn't move. The moment he relaxed the breath in his chest, in the blink of an eye, Lu Wei was passed by several people one by one, finally falling to the tail end of the second tier, struggling to hang on.

Li Luo didn't pay much attention to Lu Wei; he just looked at the back of the person in first place.

He had originally thought the other person might be a sports student.

But looking at their strength, it didn't really seem like it.

By the last lap and a half, Li Luo's body also began to feel heavy. His nasal passages and lips grew scorching hot with his fervent breathing.

His chest was like a bellows, huffing and puffing.

The cheers of his Class Eight classmates rang in his ears.

Countless eyes were fixed on him.

When he reached the final lap, he smoothly passed the person in front, and with the strength he still had left after conserving it for seven laps, he launched into a sprint all at once!

He crossed the finish line!

The cheers were earth-shattering!

Li Luo's mind was buzzing. He took huge gulps of fresh air, like a vagrant who had been starving for eight hundred years. His chest heaved violently, and his whole body felt incredibly weak.

Zhu Yufei and Zhang Guohuang quickly ran up, propping him up on either side. Following the P.E. teacher's instructions, they walked Li Luo slowly around the field.

"You can't sit down and rest yet. The P.E. teacher said we have to walk you around a bit more. You can only sit after you've recovered."

"I know..." Li Luo responded weakly, then couldn't help but look at Xu Youyu who had come over to congratulate him. "Senior, wasn't there supposed to be a sports student? Where is he?"

"Huh? You didn't know? That sports student sprained his ankle training two days ago, so he didn't compete." As Xu Youyu spoke, she had a sudden realization. "Oh, right, when the P.E. teacher was calling for people, you had run off to the entrance to listen to Zhusheng sing."

Li Luo: "..."

Hearing what Xu Youyu said, Yan Zhusheng's eyes flickered. She then silently walked to Li Luo's side, took out a bottle of water, twisted off the cap, and brought it to Li Luo's lips.

Li Luo didn't think much of it and opened his mouth, pouring it down to rehydrate himself.

"Class President, Class President!" Xu Yinghuan ran over from not far away, pointing towards the center of the grass field. "The people over there are calling you to receive your medal and take a group photo."

After walking on the field for about ten minutes, the guys who had been lapped by Li Luo finally finished the race.

After the rankings were calculated, Li Luo was helped to the awards podium. He stood on the highest champion's spot and received a gold medal from the P.E. teacher, which was hung around his neck.

After the photoshoot ended, surrounded by his Class Eight classmates, Li Luo returned to his seat in the stands and let out a long sigh, thinking about finishing the bottle of water from just now.

But when he turned his head, he watched with wide eyes as Yan Zhusheng unscrewed that same bottle of water and tilted her head back, drinking it glug-glug.

"Hey, wait..." Li Luo's eyes widened. "Isn't that my water?"

"Huh?" Yan Zhusheng froze for a moment. "This was my water to begin with. I just saw you were thirsty and let you have a sip."

Hearing Yan Zhusheng say something so innocent and guileless, Li Luo fell silent for a moment, unable to speak for a long time.

(End of this chapter)
